items.title: Where healthcare could sway voters, organizers ramp up an old tactic: talking to people
items.summary: In Wisconsin, voters weigh candidates who backed cuts to Medicaid, and those who want to expand itGoing door to door in western Wisconsin multiple times per week, Bill Hogseth tells strangers about his seizure.Hogseth, the co-executive director and lead organizer of the nonpartisan group GrassRoots Organizing Western Wisconsin (Groww), tells them about waking up in an ambulance, and the impact of the seizure on his ability to drive and work.

items.title: As online dating goes into ‘salvage mode’, can AI solve all its problems?
items.summary: Dating apps such as Bumble forced to adapt as ‘swipe fatigue’ growsBumble was supposed to be different. When it launched in 2014, it offered women a simple proposition: if you matched with a man, you had to make the first move. The rule was meant to make online dating safer and less intimidating, while giving women control over who got to speak first.This week, Bumble abandoned it. Continue reading...
